contribution.value: Proposes PagedAttention, an attention algorithm that stores KV cache in non-contiguous paged blocks like OS virtual memory, and builds vLLM, a serving system that yields 2-4x throughput over FasterTransformer and Orca.

ev.quote: we propose PagedAttention, an attention algorithm inspired by the classical virtual memory and paging techniques in operating systems. On top of it, we build vLLM, an LLM serving system that achieves (1) near-zero waste in KV cache memory and (2) flexible sharing of KV cache within and across requests
We synthesize workloads based on ShareGPT [51] and Alpaca [50] datasets, which contain input and output texts of real LLM services.
We synthesize workloads based on ShareGPT [51] and Alpaca [50] datasets
we use the WMT16 [4] Englishto-German translation dataset and synthesize two prefixes that include an instruction and a few translation examples

data_size.value: 1-hour synthetic Poisson traces (15 minutes for OPT-175B); ShareGPT inputs/outputs ~8.4x and ~5.8x longer than Alpaca on average

ev.quote: the ShareGPT dataset has 8.4× longer input prompts and 5.8× longer outputs on average than the Alpaca dataset, with higher variance ... we evaluate the systems with 1-hour traces. As an exception, we use 15-minute traces for the OPT-175B model
We use OPT [62] models with 13B, 66B, and 175B parameters and LLaMA [52] with 13B parameters for our evaluation.
We use OPT [62] models with 13B, 66B, and 175B parameters
We use OPT [62] models with 13B, 66B, and 175B parameters
and LLaMA [52] with 13B parameters for our evaluation

eval_metrics.value: Normalized latency (mean end-to-end latency divided by output length)

ev.quote: we measure normalized latency of the systems, the mean of every request's end-to-end latency divided by its output length
vLLM can sustain 1.7×–2.7× higher request rates compared to Orca (Oracle) and 2.7×–8× compared to Orca (Max)
Average number of batched requests when serving OPT-13B for the ShareGPT (2 reqs/s) and Alpaca (30 reqs/s) traces
We show 6.1% - 9.8% memory saving on parallel sampling and 37.6% - 55.2% on beam search
We visualize the average percentage of memory wastes in our experiments in Fig. 2, revealing that the actual effective memory in previous systems can be as low as 20.4%.
this leads to 20–26% higher attention kernel latency, compared to the highly-optimized FasterTransformer implementation

key_results.value: vLLM yields 2-4x throughput improvement over FasterTransformer and Orca at the same level of latency

ev.quote: vLLM improves the throughput of popular LLMs by 2-4× with the same level of latency compared to the state-of-the-art systems, such as FasterTransformer and Orca

key_results.value: On ShareGPT, vLLM sustains 1.7-2.7x higher request rates than Orca (Oracle) and 2.7-8x higher than Orca (Max); up to 22x higher than FasterTransformer

ev.quote: vLLM can sustain 1.7×–2.7× higher request rates compared to Orca (Oracle) and 2.7×–8× compared to Orca (Max), while maintaining similar latencies ... vLLM can sustain up to 22× higher request rates

key_results.value: Beam search with width 6 on OPT-13B/Alpaca: improvement over Orca (Oracle) grows from 1.3x (basic sampling) to 2.3x; KV memory savings of 37.6-55.2%

ev.quote: The improvement of vLLM over Orca (Oracle) on OPT-13B and the Alpaca dataset goes from 1.3× in basic sampling to 2.3× in beam search with a width of 6 ... 37.6% - 55.2% on beam search

key_results.value: Shared-prefix translation (LLaMA-13B, WMT16): 1.67x throughput over Orca (Oracle) for 1-shot prefix, 3.58x for 5-shot prefix

ev.quote: vLLM achieves 1.67× higher throughput than Orca (Oracle) when the one-shot prefix is shared. Furthermore, when more examples are shared (Fig. 16 (b)), vLLM achieves 3.58× higher throughput than Orca (Oracle)

key_results.value: Existing systems waste ~80% of KV cache memory; only 20.4-38.2% of KV cache stores actual token states

ev.quote: our profiling results in Fig. 2 show that only 20.4% - 38.2% of the KV cache memory is used to store the actual token states in the existing systems
we build vLLM, an LLM serving system that achieves (1) near-zero waste in KV cache memory and (2) flexible sharing of KV cache within and across requests
we propose PagedAttention, an attention algorithm inspired by the classical virtual memory and paging techniques in operating systems
Model size | 13B | 66B | 175B | GPUs | A100 | 4×A100 | 8×A100-80GB | Total GPU memory | 40 GB | 160 GB | 640 GB
we use A2 instances with NVIDIA A100 GPUs on Google Cloud Platform

value.baseline: FasterTransformer and Orca (state-of-the-art LLM serving systems)

ev.quote: vLLM improves the throughput of popular LLMs by 2-4× with the same level of latency compared to the state-of-the-art systems, such as FasterTransformer and Orca

strengths.value: Cuts KV cache memory waste from ~80% to near zero, allowing 2-4x more requests per batch on the same GPU.

ev.quote: vLLM, an LLM serving system that achieves (1) near-zero waste in KV cache memory and (2) flexible sharing of KV cache within and across requests to further reduce memory usage

strengths.value: Enables flexible KV cache sharing across sequences for parallel sampling, beam search, and shared prefixes via copy-on-write.

ev.quote: vLLM enables the sharing of most of the space used to store the prompts' KV cache across multiple output samples, with the exception of the final logical block, which is managed by a copy-on-write mechanism

strengths.value: Open-source code released; widely adopted backbone for LLM serving research and production.

ev.quote: vLLM's source code is publicly available at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm

strengths.value: Throughput gains scale with longer sequences, larger models, and more complex decoding algorithms.

ev.quote: The improvement is more pronounced with longer sequences, larger models, and more complex decoding algorithms

weaknesses.value: PagedAttention adds 20-26% overhead to the attention kernel versus the highly-optimised FasterTransformer kernel.

ev.quote: this leads to 20–26% higher attention kernel latency, compared to the highly-optimized FasterTransformer implementation

weaknesses.value: Authors note paging benefits do not generalise: workloads with static shapes or compute-bound serving may see no gain or a slowdown.

ev.quote: in serving DNNs that are not LLMs, an increase in memory efficiency may not result in any performance improvement since the performance is primarily compute-bound. In such scenarios, introducing the vLLM's techniques may rather degrade the performance

weaknesses.value: Swapping recovery suffers from small-block PCIe overhead; recomputation only matches it for medium block sizes.

ev.quote: swapping incurs excessive overhead with small block sizes. This is because small block sizes often result in numerous small data transfers between CPU and GPU, which limits the effective PCIe bandwidth

weaknesses.value: Block-size choice is a tradeoff: too small underutilises GPU, too large increases internal fragmentation and reduces sharing.

ev.quote: If the block size is too small, vLLM may not fully utilize the GPU's parallelism for reading and processing KV cache. If the block size is too large, internal fragmentation increases and the probability of sharing decreases

limitations.value: Evaluated only on data-centre A100 GPUs; no edge or mobile deployment is reported.

ev.quote: we use A2 instances with NVIDIA A100 GPUs on Google Cloud Platform

limitations.value: Does not quantize weights, activations, or KV cache; orthogonal to compression techniques and reports no bit-width experiments.

ev.quote: PagedAttention, a new attention algorithm that allows attention keys and values to be stored in non-contiguous paged memory

limitations.value: Safety, jailbreak, refusal, bias, or toxicity behaviour after serving optimisation is not measured.

ev.quote: vLLM improves the throughput of popular LLMs by 2-4× with the same level of latency

limitations.value: Throughput is the headline metric; energy consumption and per-token wall-clock latency are not separately reported.

ev.quote: We focus on serving throughput

future_work_stated.value: Apply vLLM's virtual memory and paging techniques to other GPU workloads with similar dynamic memory properties.

ev.quote: we would be excited to see vLLM's techniques being applied to other workloads with similar properties to LLM serving
